units: <cite ref="Chagigah 15a:11">Ib. 15ᵃ</cite> <he>מה כלי … יש להם ת׳ … יש לו ת׳</he> as gold and glass vessels, even when they are broken, can be mended (remolten), so may a scholar, even if he has sinned, be restored (through repentance); <cite ref="Avot D'Rabbi Natan 24:5">Ab. d’R. N. ch. XXIV</cite>.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Shabbat 9:7:6">Y. Sabb. IX, end, 12ᵇ</cite>, v. <cite ref="P00268"><he>עוֹלָמִית</he></cite>; a. fr.

senses.gloss: arrangement, ordinance, improvement, measure for the public welfare, reform.
units: <cite ref="Ketubot 10a:3">Keth. 10ᵃ</cite> <he>הואיל ותַקָּנַת חכמים וכ׳</he> since it (the K’thubah) is merely a Rabbinical ordinance, she can collect her jointure only from the worst land.

<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 4:6">Gitt. IV, 6</cite> we must not help captives to escape, <he>מפני תקנת השבויין</he> this regulation was made for the benefit of the (remaining) captives (who would be ill-treated after one escaped).

<cite ref="Mishnah Gittin 5:5">Ib. V, 5</cite> it has been decreed that if a joist is stolen and put into a building, the owner must accept the money for it, <he>מפני תקנת השבים</he> as a measure for the benefit of repentant sinners.
<cite ref="Mishnah Rosh Hashanah 1:4">R. Hash. I, 4</cite> <he>מפני תקנת קרבן</he> in order to be able to regulate the sacrifices (for the New Year’s day).
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 115a">B. Kam. 115ᵃ</cite>, a. e. <he>תקנת השוק</he>, v. <cite ref="U00521"><he>שׁוּק</he> III</cite>.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Rosh Hashanah 4:2:2">Y. R. Hash. IV, 59ᵇ</cite> bot. <he>ויש ת׳ אחר הת׳</he> is there an ordinance after an ordinance, i.e. can a measure enacted by the Rabbis be extended by another enactment?; a. fr.—Pl. <he>תַּקָּנוֹת</he>. Bab.
<cite ref="Rosh Hashanah 31b:6">R. Hash. 31ᵇ</cite> <he>זו אחת מתשע ת׳ וכ׳</he> (not <he>אחד</he>) this is one of the nine reforms introduced by R. J. ben Zaccai.
<cite ref="Bava Kamma 82a:3">B. Kam. 82ᵃ</cite> <he>עשר ת׳ וכ׳</he> (not <he>עשרה</he>) Ezra made ten regulations: that reading from the Law should take place on Mondays and Thursdays &c.
<cite ref="Menachot 51b:20">Men. 51ᵇ</cite> <he>שתי ת׳ וכ׳</he> (not <cite ref="U01585"><he>שני</he></cite>) two reforms were introduced by the Rabbis &c.
B. Mets. 112ᵇ הני הילכתא נינהו הני ת׳ נינהו do you call these hălakhoth (legal decisions)? these are reforms (changing the Biblical law).
<cite ref="Bava Metzia 112b:3">Ib.</cite> <he>ת׳ קבועות</he> measures deserving to be perpetuated (to supersede the Biblical law); a. fr.
